description: We are building a Lunar Risk & Red Flag Analyzer for the Moon’s south pole. Instead of a basic 3D map, we are developing an automated Go/No-Go feasibility dashboard that instantly flags fatal mission risks like power starvation and direct-to-Earth communication blackouts.
summary:
To Land or Not to Land: Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an interactive 3D web application that evaluates landing feasibility at the Moon’s South Pole using NASA lunar topography (LOLA) and ephemeris data.

Unlike fragmented tools like JPL Horizons and QuickMap, our platform translates orbital geometry into instant Green, Yellow, and Red risk scores, letting users simulate launch delays, inspect Sun and Earth horizon angles, and compare sites side-by-side in real time.

Because shifting a South Pole site by meters or a launch by days can cut off solar power or Earth communications, our tool accelerates agile mission planning while making lunar exploration accessible to educators and the public.
details:
What It Does & How It Works To Land or Not to Land: Lunar Landing Site Navigator is a real-time 3D mission-planning and educational platform for evaluating landing sites at the lunar South Pole. The simulation engine computes lunar orbital geometry (including the Moon’s 1.54° axial obliquity over its 346.62-day draconic cycle and Earth’s ±6.68° / ±7.7° optical libration cycles) alongside local topography to evaluate any site-date combination. Users can inspect 9 official NASA Artemis candidate landing regions, or any custom Latitude/Longitude coordinate, scrub through a Synodic Cycle timeline to simulate launch delays, inspect local terrain relief in a 200m 3D Surface Patch view, and view exact Sun and Earth positions relative to the local horizon.

Engineering Factors Considered Every site-date evaluation dynamically scores four mission-critical lander constraints into Go (Green), Caution (Yellow), and No-Go (Red) tiers. Thresholds are live-adjustable:

• Terrain Slope: Safe (< 5°), Caution (5°–15°), Hazard (> 15° tip-over risk)

• Surface Roughness: Low, Moderate, or High boulder and crater density

• Solar Illumination: Safe (> 70% of lunar day), Caution (30%–70%), Hazard (< 30% deep shadow)

• Earth Direct Line-of-Sight (LOS): Direct LOS (> 5° elevation), Grazing LOS Caution (0°–5° diffraction risk), or Blocked (< 0° / relay required)

How Our Project Is Creative Existing lunar analysis tools require navigating fragmented interfaces and raw ephemeris tables. We unified 3D orbital vectors, adjustable RYG (Red, Yellow, Green) surface risk overlays, panoramic and polar lander horizon sky domes, and live multi-site side-by-side comparison into a single, intuitive telemetry interface.

Benefits & Intended Impact For mission planners and engineers, the tool accelerates agile "what-if" trade-off analysis when launch schedules slip or landing targets shift by hundreds of meters. Through a built-in Planner / Educator mode toggle, it also serves students, educators, and the public by visually explaining why South Pole geometry creates "Peaks of Eternal Light" next to permanently shadowed craters.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

• Frontend & 3D Engine: React, TypeScript, Three.js / WebGL, Tailwind CSS, Vite

• Physics & Risk Modeling: Custom TypeScript orbital mechanics, libration, horizon occultation, and multi-factor risk-scoring engine

• Collaboration & Source Code: GitHub (https://github.com/AdeshDeshmukh/to-land-or-not-to-land-)
